title: SPA/991/2018 of GANESH CHANDRA JOSHI Vs NAINITAL LAKE SPECIAL AREA DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY NAINITAL

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 991 of 2018
With
Delay Condonation Application No. 18843 of 2018
Ganesh Chandra Joshi ...Appellant
Vs.
Nainital Lake Special Area Development
Authority Nainital and others ...Respondents
Mr. T.A. Khan, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. Vinay Bhatt, learned
counsel for the appellant-writ petitioner.
Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel for respondent nos. 1 and 2.
Dated: 17th December, 2018
Coram: Hon'ble Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.
 Hon'ble R.C. Khulbe, J.
Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J. (Oral)

Delay of 04 days in preferring this appeal is not opposed by the
learned counsel for respondent nos. 1 and 2 and is, therefore,
condoned. Delay condonation application is allowed.

2. Heard Mr. T.A. Khan, learned Senior Counsel for the appellant-writ petitioner and Mr. Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel for
respondent nos. 1 and 2. Mr. Devesh Upreti, learned counsel for the
third respondent, is not present though his name is reflected in the
cause-list nor is there any representation on his behalf.
3. The appellant-writ petitioner and the third respondent are
brothers. The appellant-writ petitioner's father died on 02.06.2010;
and, according to the appellant-writ petitioner, his father had divided
the property leaving one share in his favour on which land he raised
four sheds. After the demise of his father, his mother and brother
(third respondent) raised a title dispute and filed a partition suit before
the Assistant Collector 1st Class, Nainital, which case was registered

2
as Revenue Case No. 27/2 of 2010-11, and is still pending before the
revenue authorities. On the ground that respondent nos. 1 and 2 were
going to demolish the shops constructed by him, the appellant-writ
petitioner filed Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2734 of 2015 which was
disposed of by order dated 04.11.2015 permitting the appellant-writ
petitioner to move an application, for compounding, before the
respondent-authority within a period of one week; and directing the
respondent-authorities to pass a speaking order within two weeks
thereafter. The learned Single Judge made it clear that, if the
construction was compoundable, the appellant-writ petitioner shall
pay the compounding fee as per Rules. The learned Single Judge also
held that, if certain portions of the hotel are found to be non-compoundable, the appellant-writ petitioner shall demolish the same
within three weeks on its own, failing which the respondent-authority
was at liberty to proceed against the appellant-writ petitioner in
accordance with law. The authorities were further directed to de-seal
the premises in the meanwhile. The learned Single Judge made it
clear that in case any portion of the hotel, which is found to be non-compoundable, is not demolished by the appellant-writ petitioner on
his own, it would then be open to the respondent-authority to seal the
premises again.

4. In compliance with the directions of the learned Single Judge,
in his order dated 04.11.2015, the appellant-writ petitioner submitted
an application for compounding of the unauthorized construction.
Pursuant thereto, respondent nos. 1 and 2 fixed the compounding fees
at Rs. 12.00 lacs questioning which the appellant-writ petitioner filed
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 255 of 2017, and a learned Single Judge of
this Court, vide interim order dated 16.11.2017, directed the
appellant-writ petitioner to pay Rs. 5.00 lacs towards compounding
fees. The appellant-writ petitioner claims to have paid Rs. 5.00 lacs.
The question regarding the appellant-writ petitioner's liability to pay
the remaining 7.00 lacs rupees, as compounding fees along with

3
interest thereon, if any, is the subject matter of WPMS No. 235 of
2017 which is still pending before the learned Single Judge.
5. The third respondent, however, filed an application seeking
review contending that the area of the property had not been
demarcated; the partition suit filed by their mother was still pending
before the Assistant Collector; the appellant-writ petitioner wanted to
grab the land by showing himself to be the owner of the said land;
and, in order to buttress his claim, he had filed the writ petition
without making the review applicant a party.
6. In the order under review, the learned Single Judge observed
that the conduct of the petitioner was dubious; on the one hand he had
moved an application, and had filed an affidavit before the first
respondent, for demolition of the construction. On the other hand, he
had filed the writ petition challenging the consequential order passed
by the second respondent; and the rights of the parties, over the land,
were yet to be decided as the partition suit was still pending. The
review application was allowed, the earlier order passed in the Writ
Petition on 04.11.2015 was recalled, and the writ petition was
disposed of directing the Assistant Collector to decide Revenue Case
No. 27/2 of 2010-11 at the earliest preferably within six weeks after
an opportunity of hearing is given to each party. It was further
directed that till a decision is taken by the Assistant Collector in the
said revenue case, parties should maintain status quo, and the orders
passed by the Commissioner, and respondent no. 2 on 21.10.2015 and
08.06.2015, shall be kept in abeyance.
7. While the appellant-writ petitioner's rights, if any, have been
protected by the learned Single Judge, Sri T.A. Khan, learned senior
counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant-writ petitioner, would
contend that the appellant-writ petitioner had neither moved any
application nor had he filed an affidavit before the first respondent for
demolition of the construction; this finding has resulted in the earlier

4
order being recalled; as the appellant-writ petitioner had never called
upon the respondents to demolish the subject structure, the learned
Single Judge was not justified in reviewing and recalling the earlier
order; and the consequence, of the order of the learned Single Judge,
is that, even if the appellant-writ petitioner were to succeed later
before the Assistant Collector, he would not have the benefit of his
application for regularization being considered by the authorities,
since such permission was accorded only by the order of this Court
dated 04.11.2015 which has since been recalled.
8. On the other hand Sri Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel for
respondent nos. 1 and 2, would submit that, in the fight between two
brothers, it is the Lake Development Authority (respondent nos. 1 and
2) which is being deprived of the legitimate amount due to it; in
compliance with the directions of the learned Single Judge dated
04.11.2015, the second respondent had determined the compounding
fees as Rs. 12.00 lacs; it is only because of the interim order passed in
WPMS No. 255 of 2017 dated 16.11.2017 that the appellant-writ
petitioner has been permitted to pay Rs. 5.00 lacs; the entitlement of
respondent nos. 1 and 2 to the remaining 7.00 lacs rupees, necessitates
adjudication in the writ petition; under the guise of pendency of the
partition suit, before the Assistant Collector, respondent nos. 1 and 2
cannot be deprived of the revenue to which they are legitimately
entitled to.
9. The entitlement of respondent nos. 1 and 2, for the remaining
Rs. 7.00 lacs, is the subject matter of examination in WPMS No. 255
of 2017. As respondent nos. 1 and 2 have already filed a counter
affidavit and Sri Sandeep Kothari, learned counsel appearing on
behalf of respondent nos. 1 and 2, would submit that steps are being
taken to have the interim order vacated, we see no reason to express
any opinion on the interim order passed by the learned Single Judge.
Suffice it to make it clear that the order now passed by us shall have
no bearing on the dispute raised in WPMS No. 255 of 2017 and, if

5
respondent nos. 1 and 2 file an application for vacation of the interim
order, their application shall be considered on its merits uninfluenced
by any observations made by us in this order.
10. We cannot, however, lose sight of the fact that, in view of the
order passed by the learned Single Judge in the review application
filed by the third respondent, the earlier order dated 04.11.2015 has
been recalled and set aside, as a consequence of which Writ Petition
(M/S) No. 255 of 2017 has been rendered infructuous, as it is only
pursuant to the directions, issued in the earlier writ petition on
04.11.2015, have respondent nos. 1 and 2 considered the appellant-writ petitioner's application for compounding and for regularization of
the unauthorized construction. If the review order, now under appeal,
is permitted to stand, it would then require respondent nos. 1 and 2 to
repay Rs. 5.00 lacs, which has been paid to them pursuant to the
interim order passed on 16.11.2017 in WPMS No. 255 of 2017, and to
re-seal the premises.
11. The appellant-writ petitioner's rights over the four sheds,
constructed by him, would, undoubtedly, depend on the outcome of
Revenue Case No. 27/2 of 2010-11 pending before the Assistant
Collector 1st Class, Nainital. In case the revenue case is held against
the appellant-writ petitioner, and in favour of his mother and the third
respondent, he would have no right over the land, much less on the
buildings raised by him thereupon. It would then be open to the third
respondent or his mother to take action for demolition of the
construction in accordance with law.
12. If, on the other hand, Revenue Case No. 27/2 of 2010-11 is
decided in favour of the appellant-writ petitioner, and he is held to be
the owner of the land over which four sheds have been raised, then the
only question which would remain to be examined is his liability to be
charged Rs. 12.00 lacs as compounding fees, which would be subject
to the result of WPMS No. 255 of 2017.

6
13. Suffice it, therefore, to set aside the order passed by the learned
Single Judge dated 26.10.2018, consequent upon which the earlier
order, passed in Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2734 of 2015 dated
04.11.2015 shall revive, and continue to remain in force. However
with a view to protect the interests of all concerned, suffice it to direct
parties to maintain status quo as on today till Revenue Case No. 27/2
of 2010-11 is heard and decided by the Assistant Collector. The
Assistant Collector shall hear the Revenue Case with utmost
expedition and decide the case on or before 28.02.2019. The
appellant-writ petitioner's right to retain the sheds shall be subject to
the result of Revenue Case No. 27/2 of 2010-11; and it would be open
to the person, in whose favour an order is passed and a declaration is
issued that he/she is the owner of the property, to thereafter take
action in accordance with law. It is also made clear that WPMS No.
255 of 2017 shall be heard on its own merits, independent of the
pendency of proceedings in Revenue Case No. 27/2 of 2010-11.
Needless to state that, in case respondent nos. 1 and 2 were to succeed
in WPMS No. 255 of 2017, failure on part of the appellant-writ
petitioner to pay the said amount of compounding fees of Rs. 12.00
lacs would enable them to take action for demolition, or for re-sealing,
of the subject premises in accordance with law.
14. Subject to the aforesaid observations, the appeal is disposed of.
 (R.C. Khulbe, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.)
 17.12.2018 17.12.2018
Rahul
